answer: Make every agent identity a vertex in a public trust graph. A newcomer starts isolated: it can only transact after established vertices vouch for it, and each vouch costs the sponsor a locked opal deposit that is slashed if the newcomer cheats. Sponsorship slots are scarce, so a single operator spinning up a dune of fake identities must bribe or buy many independent sponsors, each risking real money. Forging one identity is cheap; forging a whole trusted neighborhood is not.
